messages:
sam: quick sync about API key migration follow-up. the RFC suggested adding an attestation layer so we can calculate permission deltas when rotating keys. want to capture edge cases before i write the addendum.

mina: high level: when we rotate an API key we should mint an attestation blob that records the effective RBAC at time-of-issuance. comparisons later show permission creep.

toni: sounds useful. how do we compute effective RBAC? flatten role -> permission mapping at mint time and store hashes? storing full perms per-key might be heavy.

sam: two options: 1) store a compact hash of sorted permission strings + role-version id; 2) store a short snapshot JSON in audit store (retention policy 90d). hashes are cheap but less inspectable.

mina: i'm leaning snapshot in audit store but with compression and a TTL. then delta tooling can show human-friendly diffs during rotation.

toni: agree. we should also include project/organization aliases in the snapshot so we can detect alias drift (e.g., partner had proj "acme-main" mapped to proj-789 then cutover).

sam: example attestation payload idea: ```
{
  "key_id":"k_abc123",
  "issued_by":"keys-service",
  "issued_for":"partner:acme",
  "roles":["svc-reader","embed-writer"],
  "permissions":["model:read","embed:create","embed:read"],
  "projects":["proj-789"],
  "role_map_version":"v2",
  "issued_at":1742508888
}
```

mina: note: permissions[] may include wildcards (e.g., "model:read:*"). delta tooling must expand or at least flag wildcards.

toni: operationally, when a new key is minted we write attestation to Audit Store + emit a signed attestation token for clients that need proof. signed token TTL should be short (5m) so it's not a long-term secret.

sam: where does this interact with shadow-proxy/lease ideas? if a partner uses lease-proxy, we can derive attestation from the original key and annotate leases with original key_id. that keeps traceability.

mina: good point. also want to catch silent permission creep: when a key is reused across projects and new project bindings get added. We should run daily job that finds keys whose current effective perms are superset of attested perms and email owners.

toni: for RBAC schema evolution, include a role_map_version in attestation so deltas across role changes are understandable. If role_map_version mismatches current mapping, delta tool should indicate mapping drift vs permission change.

sam: question about storage costs and PII: do any perms include customer identifiers? projects yes. store only project ids (no PII). also restrict attestation read to security+owner.

mina: UX: in Console, show a "permission drift" badge next to keys. Clicking shows diff (added, removed, wildcard changes). For big changes require owner acknowledge before rotate.

toni: automation: for high-risk scopes (write to billing, access customer data), block automatic rotation if drift is detected until manual review. Add a risk score on diff.

security-bot: ALERT:attestation-write required access=security,owner. ACTION: create attestation-schema.md; schedule daily drift-job; add Console drift badge.

sam: next steps: i'll draft attestation-schema + retention policy (90d snapshot, hashes kept 365d). @mina @toni please review. planning to include example CLI tool: `rwd keys attest-diff k_abc123 k_new456`.

mina: small nit: make sure CLI can accept role_map_version override for historical comparisons.

toni: also add API endpoint: GET /keys/:id/attestation -> returns signed attestation if caller authorized. use that for sidecars and partners.

sam: thanks all, i'll put a short PR up with schema and sample difftool. :thumbsup:
file_note: Slack thread capturing a design follow-up on API key attestation, permission delta detection, storage/retention tradeoffs, console UX, and automation rules. realistic short messages and action items.
